If a system is partially filled with 2 liquid, depressurization can cause the formation of dry ice, which poses potential hazards. For maintenance on larger segments, it is advisable to direct as much LCO as possible into the downstream 2 system before starting the draining procedure. This approach minimizes the time needed to empty the segment and reduces CO emissions into the atmosphere. Personnel responsible for handling LCO should 2 2 follow established procedures and be well-informed about the associated hazards of these operations. A more detailed philosophy regarding the drainage of specific systems will be developed in the next phase. 4.8.4 REDUNDANCY AND SPARING PHILOSOPHY As stated elsewhere in this report, the liquefaction plant will be comprised by two trains of 50% target throughput each. In other words, each liquefaction train will be able to liquefy 1 million tons of CO per 2 year, requiring both to reach the target of 2 million tons per year. At this early stage, this philosophy of redundancy seems a reasonable compromise. With 0% redundancy, or a single 100% liquefaction train, overall CAPEX could be reduced substantially since the liquefaction trains, and specifically the 3-stage compressors, represent the largest single component of plant CAPEX. However, in that scenario the plant could risk losing substantial revenue, and risk disappointing its customer(s), since it would have to completely shut down in the event of a failure of a critical component of the single train. On the other hand, providing for 100% redundancy, or two trains each capable of the entire hub’s target throughput, would likely be prohibitively expensive. This is because the liquefaction plant cost is among the single highest line items in the CAPEX estimate, second only to the cost of the storage tanks. Doubling the capacity of the liquefaction system to achieve full 100% redundancy would add tens of millions of dollars to the CAPEX and seriously degrade the hub’s economic feasibility. With two 50% trains, a critical failure in one train would still allow the hub to receive CO from its customer(s) and keep the CO ships running, 2 2 albeit at a reduced rate. Additional plant redundancy comes in the form of the eleven storage tanks, each of which will have its own piping connections and isolation valving off the CO header coming from the liquefaction plant.
